Add Google OAuth.confidenceReason: Atlas has analyzed similar authentication flows in 2,400+ repositories
Add Google OAuth.summary: Extend the existing authentication system to support Google as an OAuth provider. The codebase already has a GitHub OAuth stub that can serve as a template.

prerequisites.description: Understand how the existing login flow processes credentials and creates sessions
The auth middleware validates tokens on every request. Your OAuth tokens must pass through this.

relevantFiles.reason: Currently only supports GitHub. Add Google provider here using the same interface pattern.
Token validation must support Google's JWT format alongside existing session tokens.
relevantFiles.warning: This file has caused 3 production incidents. It handles auth + logging + rate-limiting in one place. Webhook retries aren't tested.

relevantFiles.reason: Add Google client ID, secret, and redirect URI to OAuth configuration.
Add googleId field to user schema. This requires a database migration.
relevantFiles.warning: Uses a migration system — adding a field requires a migration file.

relevantFiles.reason: Add Google OAuth callback integration tests. Currently missing OAuth test coverage.

knownTraps.title: God Module — 3 Production Incidents
knownTraps.description: This file handles auth + logging + rate-limiting + analytics in one place. It has caused 3 production outages. The most common failure: webhook retries aren't tested, leading to duplicate session creation.
knownTraps.recommendation: Review tests/middleware.test.ts before editing. Consider splitting this file first.

knownTraps.title: Migration Required
knownTraps.description: This model uses a migration system. Adding the googleId field requires creating a new migration file, not just editing the schema.
knownTraps.recommendation: Check existing migrations in db/migrations/ for the pattern before creating a new one.

knownTraps.title: Provider Abstraction Incomplete
knownTraps.description: The current GitHub OAuth implementation is a stub without proper error handling. Don't copy its pattern directly.
knownTraps.recommendation: Add proper error handling for OAuth callback failures (user denies access, token exchange fails).

Fix login bug.confidenceReason: Atlas has identified the most common login failure patterns in this codebase
Fix login bug.summary: Debug the login flow. Based on the codebase structure, the most likely failure points are in credential validation and session creation.

relevantFiles.reason: Core login logic. Error messages are caught silently at line 72 — add console.error to surface the actual failure.
relevantFiles.warning: Errors are silently caught at L72. This hides the actual root cause.

relevantFiles.reason: Session validation may be failing silently. Check token expiry logic.
Frontend auth hook — check if token refresh has a race condition (known issue).
relevantFiles.warning: Token refresh has a known race condition when multiple tabs are open.

relevantFiles.reason: Check existing test coverage for the login flow. Missing edge case tests.

route.action: Add error logging at L72, reproduce bug
Check for race condition in token refresh
Add test for the bug scenario

knownTraps.title: Silent Error Catching
knownTraps.description: Line 72 catches all errors without logging. You won't see the actual failure unless you add explicit error output.
knownTraps.recommendation: Add console.error(err) inside the catch block before investigating further.

knownTraps.title: Token Refresh Race Condition
knownTraps.description: When multiple tabs are open, concurrent token refresh requests can invalidate each other, causing intermittent logouts.
knownTraps.recommendation: Add a mutex or use a shared BroadcastChannel to coordinate token refresh across tabs.

Add dark mode.confidenceReason: Standard theme implementation — Atlas has seen this pattern in 4,800+ repositories
Add dark mode.summary: Implement a dark mode toggle. The codebase has a theme system in place but only defines a light palette. Extend it with dark tokens and add a toggle with persistence.

prerequisites.description: Understand the existing design token structure before adding dark variants

relevantFiles.reason: Create dark palette alongside existing light theme tokens.
Update CSS custom properties to use theme tokens.

knownTraps.title: Hardcoded Colors
knownTraps.description: Some components use hardcoded hex values instead of CSS custom properties. These won't respond to theme changes.
knownTraps.recommendation: Search for hardcoded color values and replace with var(--color-*) tokens.

Improve performance.confidenceReason: Performance analysis requires runtime profiling — Atlas can identify structural issues but not runtime bottlenecks
Improve performance.summary: Address structural performance issues. The main suspects are the Dashboard component (too many re-renders), the auth middleware (blocking every request), and missing database indexes.

prerequisites.description: Understand React rendering patterns to identify unnecessary re-renders

relevantFiles.reason: 248 LOC component fetching data, managing layout, and running business logic. Likely causing excessive re-renders.
relevantFiles.warning: Monolithic component doing data fetching + layout + business logic. Split before optimizing.

relevantFiles.reason: Runs on every authenticated request. Contains analytics tracking that could be async.
Missing index on email field causes slow lookups on every login.
No connection pooling — each component creates a new WebSocket connection.

knownTraps.title: Premature Optimization Trap
knownTraps.description: Don't micro-optimize renders before splitting the component. The real issue is architectural, not algorithmic.
knownTraps.recommendation: Split first, measure second, optimize third.

lessons.title: Component Architecture
lessons.description: How the UI is structured — from atomic components (Button, Input) to composed views (Dashboard, BillingPanel)
lessons.insight: The Dashboard component is a known monolith (248 LOC). The team plans to split it — keep this in mind.

lessons.title: State Management
lessons.description: Authentication, team data, and subscriptions are managed through custom hooks
lessons.insight: useAuth has a known race condition with token refresh. There's a TODO to add mutex support.

lessons.title: Styling System
lessons.description: Design tokens in theme.ts, global styles in globals.css, component styles in components.css
lessons.insight: Some components use hardcoded colors instead of design tokens. This is tech debt — use tokens for new work.

lessons.title: API Integration
lessons.description: How the frontend communicates with the backend through route handlers and services
lessons.insight: API calls are not centralized — some components call services directly. Follow the hook pattern for new features.

lessons.title: API Routes & Middleware
lessons.description: Request lifecycle: route → middleware pipeline → handler → response
lessons.insight: The auth middleware (auth.ts) is a God module — it handles auth + logging + rate-limiting. This is the #1 risk in the codebase.

lessons.title: Database Models
lessons.description: Data layer — User, Team, Subscription, Invite, AuditLog models and their relationships
lessons.insight: Models use a migration system. Never edit the schema directly — always create a migration file.

lessons.title: Authentication
lessons.description: Login, session management, password reset, and OAuth flows
lessons.insight: OAuth currently only supports GitHub. Google OAuth is planned as the next integration.

lessons.title: Payment System
lessons.description: Stripe integration for subscriptions, billing, and webhooks
lessons.insight: HIGH RISK AREA: Webhook signature verification is custom (not using Stripe SDK). No idempotency handling. 3 prod incidents.

lessons.title: Known Fragile Files
lessons.description: Files that have caused production incidents — know these before you touch anything
lessons.insight: These 3 files account for 8 out of 12 production incidents. Always check test coverage before editing.

lessons.title: Error Handling Patterns
lessons.description: How errors are caught, logged, and propagated through the system
lessons.insight: Some catch blocks swallow errors silently (especially in login.ts:L72). Always check for hidden catches.

lessons.title: Test Coverage Gaps
lessons.description: Where tests exist, where they don't, and what to write first
lessons.insight: auth.ts middleware has 0 dedicated tests despite 3 prod incidents. This is the biggest testing gap.

lessons.title: System Overview
lessons.description: High-level architecture — frontend, backend, database, external services
lessons.insight: Monolithic architecture with clear separation between routes, models, and services. Ready for microservice extraction.

lessons.title: Authentication Architecture
lessons.description: Complete auth flow — from login form to session management to middleware validation
lessons.insight: Auth spans both frontend and backend. The useAuth hook manages client state while auth.ts handles server validation.

lessons.title: Payment Architecture
lessons.description: End-to-end billing — from UI to Stripe API to webhook processing
lessons.insight: This is the riskiest subsystem. Webhook processing is not idempotent — duplicate events cause bugs.

lessons.title: Risk Assessment
lessons.description: Where the technical debt lives and what to prioritize
lessons.insight: Top 3 risks: God middleware (auth.ts, 9.2 risk), Payment bugs (stripe.ts, 8.5 risk), Monolith dashboard (Dashboard.tsx, 7.2 risk)
